t: Glass and purple dye were Sidon's two chief industries; a considerable mound of broken Murex trunculus shells near the southern harbour shows the scale of the dye works.
Sidon's navy fought with the Persian fleet at the Battle of Salamis in 480 BCE, and from the mid-5th century BCE warships were a prominent feature of the city's coins.
Cambyses II of Persia rewarded Sidon for supporting his conquest of Egypt with the territories of Dor, Joppa and the Plain of Sharon.
dyk: The oldest testimony to words of the Phoenician language of Sidon is in the Book of Deuteronomy, which records that the Sidonians called Mount Hermon 'Sirion'.
ev: Sidon, part of the Egyptian Empire, is ruled by Zimredda during the Amarna period, as Egypt's hold on the Levant weakens and the coastal cities fight for dominance.
The Temple of Eshmun, to the Phoenician god of healing, is built north of the city near the Awali River.
After Nebuchadnezzar II's subjection of the city to the Neo-Babylonian Empire, Sidon passes to the Achaemenid Empire.
Sidon's navy plays a significant role at the Battle of Salamis, aligned with the Persian fleet against the Greeks.
Eshmunazar II reigns as 'king of the Sidonians'; his sarcophagus, found in 1855, names Eshmun and Baal Sidon as the chief gods of the city.
Artaxerxes III invades Phoenicia at the end of the Persian era.
Alexander the Great occupies Sidon, beginning its Hellenistic period.

f.predecessor: The Bronze Age city and kingdom of Sidon, trading with Egypt from the Middle Bronze Age
f.successor: Hellenistic Sidon under Alexander the Great and the Diadochi, the kingdom of Abdalonymus; later the Roman Colonia Aurelia Pia Sidon
